headline: Medium-risk pair: shared file/workspace and RAG-style ingestion create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error pathways; no direct evidence of isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: caveman can use MCP and touches CLAUDE.md, project notes, and memory files; kotaemon ingests documents/HTML/PDFs and exposes a web UI. If caveman writes attacker-controlled content into shared files that kotaemon later indexes or displays, instructions can cross the boundary. The pairwise pathway is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF caveman and kotaemon share any filesystem path that kotaemon indexes or renders
IF caveman writes prompt-like text into CLAUDE.md, project notes, or memory files
mitigations: Separate their working directories
Disable automatic indexing of shared notes
Add a provenance banner to imported files
Review any shared markdown before ingestion
requires-engineering: enforce content provenance tags across the pipeline

B_data_leakage.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while kotaemon handles documents, chat transcripts, and API keys and can call external LLM APIs. If they share a workspace, sensitive content from caveman can flow into kotaemon's uploads or prompts. The profiles do not prove a shared directory, so this is inferred but plausible.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same workspace or export folder
IF kotaemon sends imported file contents to a third-party API
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared folders
Use separate OS users or containers
Turn off cloud-backed models for sensitive docs
Audit imported files for tokens before indexing
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning before API calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances, and caveman can use MCP while kotaemon writes to ./ktem_app_data and requests Docker privileges. Overlapping writes to shared mutable resources could race or corrupt state if orchestrated together. No locking mechanism is documented, so the conflict remains plausible in default deployments.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or database
IF the orchestrator does not provide file locking
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Run only one writer per resource
Use per-agent containers
Check for lockfile support in the orchestrator
requires-engineering: add transactional writes or mutexes

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman produces project notes and CLAUDE.md content that kotaemon can ingest as documents or chat transcripts. If kotaemon treats those outputs as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can propagate into downstream answers or actions. The pair lacks documented verification between producer and consumer, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF kotaemon indexes caveman-generated notes without a verification step
IF downstream users act on kotaemon answers derived from those notes
mitigations: Mark caveman output as untrusted
Require citation checks before answering
Keep generated notes separate from source docs
Sample-check retrieved passages
requires-engineering: add verification gates before action-taking

E_compliance.rationale: caveman stores session logs and memory files, while kotaemon handles API keys and chat transcripts and may send content to OpenAI/Azure/Cohere/Groq. If regulated or secret-bearing data is placed into kotaemon, retention and residency obligations can diverge from caveman's local note workflow. The profiles do not specify jurisdictions, so this is a compliance-risk inference rather than a proven violation.
conditions: IF regulated data or secrets are imported into kotaemon
IF external model APIs retain prompts or documents beyond caveman's local policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of external APIs
Document retention settings for each backend
Use local-only models for sensitive corpora
Separate secret-bearing projects from shared notes
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls
